Replace $cell.meta on a NICHESObject

Source: R/add_cell_meta.R
add_cell_meta.Rd

Fully replaces niches.obj$cell.meta with new.meta and (by default) rebuilds $edge.meta so the new columns propagate as Sending.* / Receiving.* / Joint.* columns on every edge.

The replacement is complete: any column present in the existing $cell.meta but absent from new.meta is dropped. The user is responsible for supplying all columns they wish to retain, including spatial coordinates (x, y).

new.meta must cover every cell in niches.obj$cell.list. Extra rows (cells not in $cell.list) are silently dropped with a message when verbose = TRUE.

Usage

add_cell_meta(niches.obj, new.meta, rebuild.edge.meta = TRUE, verbose = TRUE)

Arguments

niches.obj

A NICHESObject.

new.meta

A data.frame or data.table with either a "cell" column or rownames matching barcodes in niches.obj$cell.list.

rebuild.edge.meta

Logical. If TRUE (default), regenerates niches.obj$edge.meta via .build_edge_meta() so new metadata columns appear on each edge. Set to FALSE when calling repeatedly in batch – call once manually at the end.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE (default), emits messages for dropped extra cells and stale aggregation slots.

Value

Updated NICHESObject.

See also

add_meta_column to append or overwrite a single column without replacing the full table; add_neighborhood_composition and aggregate_NICHESObject to recompute stale aggregations.

Examples

# \donttest{
data(NICHESv2_example)

# Build a complete replacement metadata table
new.meta <- data.frame(
  cell     = NICHESv2_example$cell.list,
  x        = NICHESv2_example$cell.meta$x,
  y        = NICHESv2_example$cell.meta$y,
  celltype = NICHESv2_example$cell.meta$celltype,
  region   = sample(c("core", "edge"),
                    length(NICHESv2_example$cell.list),
                    replace = TRUE),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
obj.updated <- add_cell_meta(NICHESv2_example, new.meta)

# New column propagates to edges
head(obj.updated$edge.meta[, c("SendingCell", "ReceivingCell",
                               "Joint.region")])
#>    SendingCell ReceivingCell Joint.region
#>         <char>        <char>       <char>
#> 1:     Cell_10        Cell_1    edge|core
#> 2:     Cell_10       Cell_10    edge|edge
#> 3:     Cell_10       Cell_14    edge|core
#> 4:     Cell_10       Cell_25    edge|core
#> 5:     Cell_10        Cell_4    edge|core
#> 6:     Cell_10        Cell_6    edge|edge
# }
